title: Three Southern soldiers follow Billie and Simmons to the White Rose
summary: The soldiers followed them but left when they saw the mixed crowd.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: No, no, not the same night. This is another occasion. This was just the happenings of the streets you know.

So one night, another night, not the same night, Billie and I decided to walk to Fifth Avenue around 51st and come back and we'd each smoke a joint, you know, a piece coming back and when we got back, we stopped about three doors short of Sixth Avenue. And she sit on sort of a stone stoop, you know before you walk up the steps and here come three big huge southern soldiers walking down 51st Street towards Sixth Avenue and they passed by us. "Boy, that girl's pretty! Sure wish we had her down home," say, "in fact, we ought to take her right now." I say "yeah, why don't you try it?" I'm talking to these three bruisers. Because I know she's going to fight with me if I have to fight. (Laughter). So we got up and started to walking, we walked on around and walked into the White Rose and they followed us to the White Rose. And when they looked in the White Rose and saw what was happening, (laughter) this is like a Black Man in the south peeping in a restaurant seeing if they served Black men. They looked in there and saw all this conglomeration of colors and ethnic groups, I invited them and said come on in. (Laughter). They walked out.
